Prevention: Select fields which are free from termite mounds.
Deep plough the field during land preparation to expose termites to sun and predators.
Remove, burn and bury undecomposed plant residues.
Avoid injuring the plants, especially during weeding.
Incorporate all decomposed crop residues into the soil.
Destroy all wilted and stunted plants by burning and burying.
Practice mulching with manure, wood ash or tobacco waste to reduce termite infestation.
Monitoring: Uproot wilted and stunted plants to check for termite infestations.
During the growing period make frequent visits to observe crops grown close to termite mounds.
Inspect the field at least twice a week during dry spells to check for the presence of termites or termite nests and colonies.
At maturity, check for signs of scarification of pods caused by termites.
Look for wilted/dead plants, tunnels built of soil, and feeding marks underneath the tunnels.
Inspect the field during off-season to check for termite nests, mounds and colonies.
Direct Control: Dig up termite mounds and expose and destroy the queen.
